mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 2.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS level (p > 0.05) in the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS increases by at least 10% in the same month
failure_condition: In a robust labor market regime, the 20-day forward return is not statistically significantly different from zero (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate exceeds 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, the forward return is negative despite the CPIAUCSL momentum (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% while the S&P 500 20-day forward return remains positive indicates that supply-side weakness does not outweigh demand factors, suggesting a supportive macro environment for equities over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO contraction exceeds 2% and SPX 20-day forward return is negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5%, it predicts a temporary liquidity injection into financial markets, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the 20-day window following the signal (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in job openings (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 in a month while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) remains below 4% creates a labor market imbalance that boosts investor sentiment, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In tight labor markets, the 60-day forward return is not significantly higher than in loose markets (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of accelerating consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% trigger central bank policy uncertainty, which in the current policy regime (FEDFUNDS < 3%) is associated with a 5-day negative S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 3% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the identified regime.

mechanism_narrative: A statistically significant negative cross-correlation (lag -1) between S&P 500 20-day returns and the 1-month change in UNRATE indicates that falling unemployment (or rising labor demand) precedes equity market gains, holding across all macro regimes.
failure_condition: The cross-correlation is not statistically significant at the 5% level (p > 0.05) in any 12-month rolling window.
